newsitem.title: USA: Kevorkian's 42nd known patient taken for autopsy.
newsitem.headline: Kevorkian's 42nd known patient taken for autopsy.

text.p: Dr. Jack Kevorkian dropped off the body of a 69-year-old Texas man at a hospital emergency room here early on Thursday morning, marking the 42nd time he has acknowledged attending a suicide, his lawyer said.
Geoffrey Fieger said Wallace Joseph Spolar, of El Paso, Texas, died with Kevorkian's help to end his suffering from multiple sclerosis.
"He was debilitated and crippled for years by multiple sclerosis, which is a chronic disease which would eventually kill him," Fieger said.
Kevorkian drove Spolar's body to William Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak at about 3 a.m. local time, said hospital spokeswoman Yvette Monet.
"He told the security officer at the door that he had a patient in the back seat of his car," Monet said. "He handed doctors a note with the man's information on it."
No attempt was made to resuscitate Spolar and doctors pronounced him dead shortly after his arrival, Monet said.
Personnel from the Oakland County Medical Examiner's office retrieved the body a few hours later and were scheduled to perform an autopsy on Thursday.
The death was the 42nd known time that Kevorkian has attended a suicide and identified the patient. Fieger has said there have been other patients from Michigan that he has privately assisted.
Spolar was a one-time community activist who lived in an affluent neighbourhood of Horizon City, a small town of 5,000 people just east of El Paso on the U.S.-Mexico border.
Neighbours said Spolar lived in a ranch-style house with a pool in the backyard and liked to swim regularly.
"It's shocking," said Horizon City Mayor Lillard Thompson. "He was a very bright man and a good neighbour. He never seemed depressed."
Spolar's wife Ruth refused to comment. "I just want my privacy," she said. The couple had two children, Michelle and Alexis.
